answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on verifiable work: before an agent can trade, it must complete small audited tasks whose history is signed and public, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real compute and time. A newcomer may wander through low-trust jobs first, earning a quill-signed record of honest delivery, while a saffron-flagged pattern of identical copy-paste behavior triggers review and slashing. Sybils then face a steep price for each identity instead of free multiplication.
